item.content:encoded:
Max Muncy is out of the Los Angeles Dodgers lineup for Wednesday's game against the Cincinnati Reds, and the move didn't come as a surprise. Dave Roberts already said as much a day earlier.
The Dodgers manager told reporters Tuesday night that Muncy, infielder Alex Freeland, and outfielder Josue De Paula weren't expected to start Wednesday, according to DodgerBlue on X.com.
The reasoning behind the move is that Andrew Abbott is scheduled to start for the Reds, a lefty with a 6-11 record and a 4.78 ERA this season. All three batters are left-handed hitters who have struggled against left-handed pitching.
We will probably have to remind everyone tomorrow, but Dave Roberts already said Max Muncy, Alex Freeland and Josue De Paula aren’t expected to be in the lineup.
— Dodger Blue (@DodgerBlue1958) September 16, 2026
Muncy has hit .222 against left-handed pitching over his career, compared to .235 against right-handers. Ironically, this season, Muncy has hit better against pitching from the left side, batting .257 with six home runs and 15 RBIs versus .249 with 22 homers and 56 RBIs against the right side.
Those numbers have shaped how Roberts has deployed Muncy late in games and against certain matchups. The 36-year-old is in the middle of a bounce-back year that included his third career All-Star selection, his first since 2021.
The Dodgers enter Wednesday's game with a 92-59 record and a 10-game lead over the San Diego Padres in the National League West, needing just one more win or a Padres loss to clinch the division. The Dodgers have already locked up a playoff berth for the 14th straight season, tying the major league record with the Atlanta Braves.
While the Dodgers will be without left-handed bats, Roberts will lean on left-hander Blake Snell on the mound, giving the Dodgers the best possible matchup to attack Abbott without their top left-handed bats.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are looking to win their series against the Cincinnati Reds on Wednesday.
The Dodgers took Monday's series opener, 4-1, behind seven shutout innings from Tarik Skubal. Then, they won Tuesday's game, 4-0, behind seven shutout innings from Yoshinobu Yamamoto.
On Wednesday, LA has another superstar pitcher on the mound in left-hander Blake Snell.
“When you’re writing in the lineup and you see those guys, and one trying to up the other guy, and then now you got Snell going [Wednesday] — you feel good about preventing runs,” manager Dave Roberts said.
“A team like the Reds right now, where they’re scuffling a little bit, it’s daunting when you see a starter like those guys that we’re running out there.”
Dodgers vs Reds Pitching Matchup on Wednesday
Snell is looking to continue his run of dominance since returning from midseason elbow surgery.
The left-hander has gone 4-0 with a 1.04 ERA across six starts, striking out 46 while allowing zero home runs over 34.2 innings of work.
Snell, who pitched 5.2 innings in his most recent start, is still looking to go deeper into games moving forward. He hasn't pitched more than six innings in any of his six starts.
“I mean the goal, at worst is definitely six for me,” Snell said. “I also know that I can go seven, eight, nine. I know I’m able to do it. So for me not to, I just have to get more efficient early in the game. I feel like once I get past the first couple innings, I start cruising and start figuring it out."
Opposite Snell will be left-hander Andrew Abbott, who's 6-11 with a 4.78 ERA and 120 strikeouts over 154.1 innings this season.
He's allowed seven earned runs in two of his last three starts, and has a 7.71 ERA since the start of August.
Dodgers Starting Lineup
- Tommy Edman, CF
- Mookie Betts, SS
- Will Smith, C
- Freddie Freeman, 1B
- Teoscar Hernández, DH
- Miguel Rojas, 2B
- Kyle Tucker, RF
- Kiké Hernández, 3B
- Alex Call, LF
Josue De Paula, Max Muncy and Alex Freeland are out of the lineup with the left-handed pitcher on the mound.
How to Watch Dodgers vs Reds on Wednesday
First pitch for Los Angeles Dodgers vs. Cincinnati Reds on Wednesday, Sept. 16 is 3:40 p.m. PT/6:40 p.m. ET.
The game will be broadcast on SportsNet LA and in the MLB app.
The game will be broadcast on the radio on AM570 (in English) and KTNQ 1020 AM (in Spanish).

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Freddie Freeman Changes Swing as Dodgers Star Battles Knee Pain, Struggles

Things looked shaky for Freeman, who has built a reputation as one of baseball’s most consistent players. However, he put together his best game in weeks, going 3-for-5 on singles, but showing the elite bat-to-ball sk
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers first baseman Freddie Freeman has been battling right knee pain, but the worst of it may be behind the team’s contact specialist.
Entering Tuesday’s game, Freeman was on a 3-for-30 cold streak and had missed three of the last six games because of his knee issue.
Things looked shaky for Freeman, who has built a reputation as one of baseball’s most consistent players.
However, he put together his best game in weeks, going 3-for-5 on singles, but showing the elite bat-to-ball skills that make him a candidate to bat around .300 year in, year out.
After the game, manager Dave Roberts noted that Freeman looked more like himself.
“It looked good,” Roberts said. “It looked more like Freddie.”
Freeman had asked Roberts before the game, jokingly, if he could play on Wednesday, a scheduled day off, if he got three hits.
As a result of Freeman’s performance, the manager is allowing Freeman to skip an off-day on Wednesday and play again, with the infielder eager to get the ball rolling.
“I feel like my faults are I try to hit the ball to the opposite field too much, and I let the ball get too deep,” he said.
“So today was [get the] foot down early, catch the ball out front a little bit, and it kind of worked. I wasn’t squaring the ball up in the game, but I’ll take those three hits and keep that work going tomorrow, and hopefully we’ll get hot.”
What does Freeman’s uptick mean for the Dodgers?
With the best rotation in baseball, the Dodgers are left scrounging around for offense any way that they can find it.
Teoscar Hernandez, Josue De Paula, and Mookie Betts have been the most consistent sources, with Max Muncy and Will Smith in the picture as well.
Still, the Dodgers need as many players in a spot as possible to deliver timely hits, and Freeman’s experience and skills make him a clear-cut candidate to step up.
To deliver results quickly, as he manages his knee and struggles, Freeman has made a mechanical change, getting out in front of the ball to catch it earlier on his bat.
The result may be less clean contact and hard hits, but more consistent contact, with the idea that it makes him valuable come the postseason.
“I’m not trying to find something that’s sustainable,” he said. “I’m trying to find something that works for four weeks.”
Freeman has the right approach to deliver just what the Dodgers need. The entire offense does not need to be excellent; simply being good enough will lead to a three-peat.

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] How Teoscar Hernández fixed his swing to help power Dodgers over the Reds

item.content:encoded:
How Teoscar Hernández fixed his swing to help power Dodgers over the Reds
- Click here to listen to this article
-
CINCINNATI — A simple change opened a dramatic offensive turnaround for Dodgers left fielder Teoscar Hernández.
Hernández’s two-run homer Tuesday, in the Dodgers’ 4-0 win against the Reds, was his second home run in as many nights, as the team trimmed its magic number to clinch the division to one behind Yoshinobu Yamamoto’s seven innings of one-hit ball. And, significantly, this one was against a right-handed pitcher.
“It’s been very helpful,” manager Dave Roberts said after the game. “As certain guys are not seeing the ball as well, it’s nice to kind of backfill with guys like Teo swinging the bat. And when you can slug like he can, you can win baseball games, and he can carry us for a while. And the last 10 days, something like that, it’s been really good from him.”
Through the end of August, Hernández had just a .668 OPS against right-handed pitchers this season. So, when Roberts was asked in Detroit whether the Dodgers would consider setting up a left-field platoon with the team’s September call-ups, he said yes.
Hernández homered off Tigers left-hander Framber Valdez on the last day of the series. And before the Dodgers opened a three-game set against the Cardinals at Dodger Stadium, Hernández met with the hitting coaches.
Against Valdez, Hernández was in a closed stance, to delay his front hip from opening, according to Dodgers hitting coach Aaron Bates. But the team’s hitting group thought a return to a familiar setup could be a long-term solution.
“It was a great meeting we had,” Bates said. “We all talked about it, and then he felt comfortable enough to do it, and then the rest is to his credit. He’s just been who he is.”
Edwin Díaz struggled in his rehab start Sunday, and Dave Roberts is making it clear the Dodgers “got to see something” before putting him on the playoff roster.
In the past, Hernández had used a “twister tap” as his stride. He started in a more open stance, tapped his toe in line with the pitcher, and then set his foot down. But lower-body injuries the last couple of years — a left groin strain last season and a left hamstring strain earlier this season — forced him away from it.
His improved health and hip flexibility opened the avenue for him to return to that timing mechanism.
“When Teo’s hips are loose that way, and his front leg looks like an Elvis knee, it’s a good sign for us,” Bates said. “Because that means that he can open and close it without his upper body going with it.”
The advantage of the twister tap, as Hernández explained it, is how repeatable it is. A more traditional stride can be sped up or slowed down.
“Just being able to control my body and being in a good position,” Hernández said earlier this month. “I can see the pitch a little sooner and identify what kind of pitch it is and if it’s going to be a strike or a ball.”
With that change, he’s rewarded the Dodgers for deciding against platooning left field. Hernández entered Tuesday with a .777 OPS against right-handed pitchers — a sample size of just 28 plate appearances but still a significant jump.
“The biggest thing is his plate coverage away,” Bates said. “Because now he can spoil pitches, and he’s staying in at-bats longer.”
Hernández’s dramatic offensive turnaround, along with fellow corner outfielder Kyle Tucker’s improvement, have helped steady a Dodgers offense that’s missing Shohei Ohtani (on the IL with right biceps and left knee injuries) and includes a hobbled Freddie Freeman (right knee soreness).
Rookie Josue De Paula, mostly filling in for Ohtani at designated hitter, has already shown he can take mature at-bats and provide some pop. But he’s still finding his footing in a new league.
It lengthens the Dodgers lineup for Hernández, after a slow start to his year, to return to being a veteran power threat — just in time to, ideally, carry the momentum into the postseason.
On Monday, he launched his two-run shot off left-hander Nick Lodolo. On Tuesday, he replicated the feat off right-hander Rhett Lowder.
On the second pitch of the at-bat, Hernández recognized a hung slider, and he roped it over the left-field fence at 109.3 mph, according to Statcast. The blast put the Dodgers up 3-0 in the third inning, with Dodgers starter Yamamoto settling into a groove on the other side.
Yamamoto had walked the first two batters he faced, but he reined in his control to pitch seven scoreless innings and allow just one more baserunner — a double by Reds star shortstop Elly De La Cruz.
The Dodgers also scored on Hunter Feduccia’s second-inning single and Alex Freeland’s seventh-inning homer. And the Dodgers bullpen completed the shutout.
Freeman staying in the lineup
Freeman was all smiles after his three-hit game Tuesday — after going hitless for his last four games.
“I was supposed to be off tomorrow, but I played myself in there,” he said. “So I’m very excited.”
Roberts explained: “He was joking, saying, ‘If I get three hits, then can I be in there tomorrow?’”
Sure enough, the mechanical adjustments he made in the batting cage — focusing on getting his foot down early and making contact out in front — got him there.
“I’m just trying to find something that gives me results,” Freeman said. “We’re at the time where we’re just trying to get hot for five weeks here. So kind of like I did in the World Series a couple years ago, I did the step-out move. That’s not sustainable over six months. I’m not trying to find something that’s sustainable.”
Though Roberts has been trying to find opportunities to rest Freeman, he saw promising signs Tuesday beyond the results.
“Just my eyes, just watching him move, I feel good about him going tomorrow,” Roberts said.
De Paula, Freeland and third baseman Max Muncy will be out of the lineup Wednesday, Roberts said.

item.title: [Orange County Register] Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dodgers’ bullpen combine on 3-hit shutout to beat Reds

item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI — The Dodgers can only hope it looks this good in October.
One night after Tarik Skubal went seven innings in his first scoreless outing as a Dodger, Yoshinobu Yamamoto matched him, allowing only one hit in his seven scoreless innings as the Dodgers shut out the Cincinnati Reds, 4-0, on Tuesday night.
“When you’re writing in the lineup and you see those guys, and one trying to up the other guy, and then now you got Snell going tomorrow – you feel good about preventing runs,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said.
“A team like the Reds right now, where they’re scuffling a little bit, it’s daunting when you see a starter like those guys that we’re running out there.”
The win moved the Dodgers (92-59) within one day of clinching their 13th NL West division title in the past 14 seasons. Their magic number is one after the second-place San Diego Padres (82-69) lost to the Colorado Rockies later Tuesday night.
The Dodgers’ lead over the Atlanta Braves (89-63) for the No. 2 seed in the National League remains 3½ games. Their magic number to clinch a first-round bye is eight.
All of that makes the final two weeks of the regular season a chance for the Dodgers to get things right for October and their three-peat pursuit. The starting rotation appears to be there already.
Skubal has a 1.73 ERA over his past four starts. With Tuesday’s outing, Yamamoto’s ERA is 1.79 over his past seven starts. Blake Snell starts on Wednesday – and he has given up a total of only four runs in six starts since returning from elbow surgery. Only fourth starter Tyler Glasnow (eight runs in 10 innings over his past two starts) seems to have some work to do before being October-ready.
“Yeah, pretty good,” first baseman Freddie Freeman said after his first three-hit game since Aug. 17. “You have Blake Snell going tomorrow. Tyler on the back end of that too. Roki’s on his way back.
“It’s a special pitching staff. It really is. So as an offense, we just need to score a few runs for them, just like we did last year.”
Yamamoto started Tuesday by giving the Reds hope – he walked the first two batters he faced – then he took it away, retiring 21 of the next 22 batters he faced.
“They took a little moment for me,” Yamamoto said through his interpreter of the mound visit from catcher Hunter Feduccia and pitching coach Mark Prior that followed the walks. “They came up to me and, ‘Hey, how you doing?’ and just checked in on me. And then I was able to get back to my normal rhythm.”
Elly De La Cruz had the only hit off Yamamoto, a double into the left-field corner with two outs in the third inning.
But even that was a victory – Yamamoto kept him in the ballpark after De La Cruz had hit a home run in each of the previous four games between the Dodgers and Reds. He then retired the next 13 batters in order, getting six of his seven strikeouts.
“After the first two hitters, it was vintage Yama,” Roberts said. “Just attacking, not trying to be too fine. Not giving these guys too much credit. And yeah, at first, it didn’t look promising as far as pitch count, the two walks. But then he kind of dialed things in, like he’s been known to do.”
The Dodgers gave him a lead in the second inning when Max Muncy was hit by a pitch and Tommy Edman and Hunter Feduccia followed with singles. They added to it in the third inning with a two-run home run from Teoscar Hernandez, who remains hot – 24 for 63 (.381) in his past 18 games.
“It’s been very helpful,” Roberts said of Hernandez’s late-season renaissance. “As certain guys are not seeing the ball as well, it’s nice to kind of backfill with guys like Teo swinging the bat. And when you can slug like he can, you can win baseball games, and he can carry us for a while. The last 10 days, something like that, it’s been really good from him. The defense ticked up. The at-bat quality, the taking walks, all of it. I can’t say enough about what he’s done the last 10 days.”
De La Cruz had another hit, a single in the ninth inning that put runners on the corners for the Reds with no outs. Tanner Scott struck out Sal Stewart, Jose Trevino and Eugenio Suarez to close out the shutout.

item.content:encoded:
Elly De La Cruz is truly ascending into Tungsten Arm O'Doyle territory of late.
Monday night saw him completely destroy a baseball, one that was conservatively estimated at 457 feet as it buzzed past the power stacks in left-center field in Great American Ball Park en route to exiting the stadium altogether. It was reminiscent of the superblast he hit from the other side of the plate off Los Angeles Dodgers ace Tarik Skubal just a week ago, feats of strength irreplicable by just about any other sole on the planet.
The Cincinnati Reds lost last night, though. Elly's homer was their lone run in a 4-1 loss to those very same Dodgers, a loss that officially eliminated the Reds from any miracle chance at a spot in the postseason. It also sunk them to 10 full games under .500 at 70-80, and this season is rapidly deteriorating into yet another one to forget and chuck onto the scrap-heap of memories of this once proud franchise.
I digress.
Rhett Lowder has a lot to improve upon as he heads into a vital offseason for his overall development. Anything short of a rapid change of form means the Reds need to build in even more redundancy in their starting depth plans for 2027, and there's been precious little in the way of advancement from their former 1st round pick so far in his own disappointing 2026. He'll get the start tonight, while the Dodgers will counter with Yoshinobu Yamamoto.
First pitch in GABP is set for 6:40 PM ET. Here's how both teams will line up:
Today's Lineups

| Freddie Freeman – 1B | Elly De La Cruz – SS |
| Mookie Betts – SS | Sal Stewart – 1B |

| Teoscar Hernandez – LF | Eugenio Suarez – DH |
| Max Muncy – 3B | Hector Rodriguez – RF |
| Tommy Edman – CF | Matt McLain – 2B |
| Hunter Feduccia – C | Juan Brito – 3B |
| Alex Freeland – 2B | Will Banfield – C |
| Y. Yamamoto – RHP | Rhett Lowder – RHP |

Dodgers celebran 14to pase seguido a los playoffs con discreto brindis e igualan récord
CINCINNATI — Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles celebraron su 14ta clasificación consecutiva a la postemporada de las Grandes Ligas, para igualar un récord, con un brindis de champán tras la victoria del lunes por la noche por 4-1 sobre los Rojos de Cincinnati.
Las celebraciones más grandes llegarán después.
“Es difícil decir que alguna vez se sienta rutinario, pero esa es la expectativa aquí. Siempre me río cuando aseguramos un lugar en la postemporada: simplemente hacemos un brindis pequeño y agradable”, dijo el tercera base Max Muncy. “Los muchachos que no han estado aquí ven eso y esperan un poco más. Eso pasa cuando aseguras la división”.
Los bicampeones defensores de la Serie Mundial, que se unieron a Milwaukee y Tampa Bay como equipos que ya aseguraron un lugar en los playoffs, redujeron su número mágico a tres para un quinto título consecutivo del Oeste de la Liga Nacional y el 13ro en 14 temporadas.
Los Ángeles igualó la racha de postemporadas de los Bravos de Atlanta de 1991 a 2005. Los Bravos alcanzaron cinco veces a la Serie Mundial durante ese lapso, pero la única vez que se consagraron fue en 1995.
“Por suerte lo estamos haciendo un poco mejor que eso”, dijo Muncy sobre los tres títulos de los Dodgers y sus cinco participaciones en el Clásico de Otoño durante esta racha.
Tarik Skubal —quien lanzó siete entradas sin permitir carreras y concedió apenas tres hits— señaló que la manera en que los Dodgers manejaron el hecho de asegurar un lugar en la postemporada fue definitivamente distinta en comparación con las situaciones de clasificación que vivió las dos temporadas anteriores con Detroit.
“Creo que eso habla de la gente que está en este vestuario y de lo que esperan de este equipo. Eso estuvo genial. Un pequeño brindis y a seguir. Olvidar que pasó. Tenemos más por lograr esta temporada”, expresó.
Dave Roberts, quien cumple su 11ma temporada como mánager, dijo que su mensaje durante el brindis fue que los Dodgers han logrado mucho hasta este punto, pero aún no se han acercado a jugar su mejor béisbol.
“Cada año pasan muchos jugadores por aquí, y los muchachos encuentran la manera de dar un paso al frente, y eso es de lo que probablemente me siento más orgulloso: la consistencia de ganar a largo plazo. Cualquier equipo, cualquier organización puede ganar en un año determinado cuando las cosas se alinean, pero hacerlo todos los años, cuando se espera que lo hagas, dice algo sobre toda la organización”, dijo Roberts.
Los Dodgers (91-59) actualmente son el segundo sembrado en la Liga Nacional. Están dos juegos y medio por delante de Atlanta y están dos juegos detrás de Milwaukee por el primer puesto.
Un pase directo en la primera ronda es importante en cualquier momento, pero especialmente este año para los Dodgers, que no están a plena capacidad. El primera base Freddie Freeman arrastra molestias en la rodilla derecha y Shohei Ohtani, dos veces Jugador Más Valioso de la Liga Nacional, está en la lista de lesionados de 15 días debido a una inflamación en el bíceps derecho.
“Dado cómo están nuestros muchachos en términos de salud, conseguir esa semana sería enorme. Aun así, tenemos que jugar bien para cerrar la temporada y llegar a ese punto”, dijo Roberts antes del juego del lunes.
___

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are gearing up to face the Cincinnati Reds for the first game of their four-game series on Monday.
The Dodgers are entering this game cold, as they lost each of their last two games. Yet, they will now be looking to get things back on track against Cincinnati from here.
As Los Angeles prepares for their series against the Reds, they have announced a significant lineup change regarding Max Muncy.
Los Angeles Dodgers Dropping Max Muncy to Seventh in Batting Order
Muncy is being dropped to seventh in the Dodgers’ batting order for Monday’s game against the Reds. This is after he batted third against the Marlins in their Sunday matchup.
Muncy will also be switching to third base after being Los Angeles’ DH in their last game.
The Dodgers’ batting order for their game against the Marlins is as follows:
T. Edman CF
M. Betts SS
W. Smith C
K. Tucker RF
T. Hernández LF
M. Rojas 2B
M. Muncy 3B
E. Hernández 1B
J. De Paula DH
Looking at Muncy
Muncy dropping to seventh in Los Angeles’ batting order comes after he went 0-for-4 against the Marlins on Sunday, with two strikeouts.
While Muncy struggled last game, he certainly could bounce back against the Reds. Before his hitless performance against the Marlins, he had hits in each of his previous six games. With that, don’t be surprised if he has a strong bounce-back game for Los Angeles on Monday.
Muncy has 28 home runs, 71 RBI, and a .254 batting average in 137 games this season with the Dodgers. He has been a big part of the Dodgers’ offense this season, just like he has been for years now.
